options: Incidents that are active AND priority 1 — equivalent to two separate addQuery calls
Incidents that are active OR priority 1
Nothing, because addEncodedQuery requires a third argument
Every incident, since addEncodedQuery is a display-only method
questions.explain: The ^ character means AND in an encoded query, exactly as it does in a list's breadcrumb — this is real executable filter input.

questions.q: What does the two-argument form `.addQuery('priority', 1)` really mean?
options: Shorthand for the three-argument form with '=' as the operator
It only works for text fields, never numeric fields
It always means 'not equal to'
It is a syntax error and must use the three-argument form
questions.explain: The two-argument form is equals by default. For any other comparison, the operator is passed explicitly as the second argument.

options: Records where assigned_to has no value (is empty)
Records where assigned_to is set to the current user
Records where assigned_to has any value at all
It deletes the assigned_to value on matching records
questions.explain: addNullQuery() filters for the field being empty. addNotNullQuery() is the opposite — filtering for the field having a value.

options: A combined condition group meaning priority 1 OR priority 2, still ANDed with any other addQuery calls
Two unrelated conditions that both must be true at once (priority equal to both 1 and 2)
A syntax error, because addOrCondition cannot be chained
Only priority 2 records, overwriting the first condition entirely
questions.explain: addOrCondition() chains an OR onto the addQuery() it's called on, forming one OR group that still combines with AND against other conditions.

questions.q: Why does `.orderBy('priority')` list Priority 1 incidents first, not last?
options: orderBy() sorts ascending, and in ServiceNow priority 1 is the most urgent (lowest number), so ascending puts it first
orderBy() always sorts by creation date regardless of the field named
Priority fields are sorted alphabetically by label, not by number
orderBy() only works on date fields, not on priority
questions.explain: orderBy() sorts ascending by the field's stored value. Since priority 1 is numerically lowest and most urgent, ascending order puts it first.
